title: Pan Grilled Pork Tenderloin
description:
Pork tenderloin is one of those items that has appeared in the last few years and it’s so versatile. Relatively inexpensive and easy to cook, pork tenderloin is very tender and succulent (if not over-cooked). Some people complain that it’s not especially tasty (no fat!), but a little sauce goes a long way. You can also buy these “pre-marinated” with BBQ or Asian flavors, but I prefer to make my own.
You can grill them quickly in a pan (as described here), outdoors on a grill (with a dry rub or spices or a BBQ or other sauce), or just roasted in the oven (25-30 minutes in a 400 degree oven). Look around, there are all kinds of other, very tasty recipes.
In a number of the dishes here, we also talk about using Pork Tenderloin medallions – like little filets, maybe pounded to flatten a bit – as a good substitute for some dishes with veal or chicken, usually with tasty sauces.
We prefer having pork more on the just barely medium side (slightly pink) which usually translates to cooking until 135 to 140 degrees and letting the meat rest for a few minutes afterwards.
Pan-Grilled Pork Tenderloin
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees.
With a sharp knife, remove any excess fat and the silver skin from the tenderloins.
Roll the tenderloins in the flour and season with some salt and pepper, as well as ground rosemary (or other spices).
ingredients: 1 teaspoon ground rosemary, thyme, garlic, or cumin
directions: Heat the oil in an oven-proof skillet almost until smoking and sear the tenderloin on medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, turning the meat over as it browns.
Add the chicken broth and white wine to the pan and place it in the oven for 10-15 minutes, until the internal temperature comes to about 135 to 140 degrees.
Remove the tenderloins to a separate dish, cover loosely with foil, and let them rest for about 10 minutes, before carving. They will continue to cook as they sit.

While the meat is resting, scrape any brown bits on the bottom of the pan and reduce the sauce a little. If it seems too thin, mix a tablespoon of cornstarch with a tablespoon of water and stir it into the sauce. Adding some butter will also thicken the sauce and add rich flavor.
Slice the pork into little steaks, pour the hot sauce over it all, and serve immediately.
